reasoning: Lagrange equations give equal cosines, hence equal triangle angles x=y=z=\pi/3. Their sine sum is 3\sqrt{3}/2; concavity of sine proves global maximality. This matches the earlier answer and Math Academy’s worked solution. The Incorrect grade applies to the submitted (3+\sqrt{3})/2, option a. Comparing with one other triangle alone is insufficient proof, but the stated maximum is correct.

answers.ma_evidence:
Therefore, the maximum value of $f$ is reached at the point $(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}),$ and the maximum value is 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
